newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe Energy wins contract in Ghana.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe Energy wins contract in Ghana.

text.p: Santa Fe Energy Resources said Wednesday it has signed a production sharing contract with the Ghana's mining and energy ministry and the Ghana National Petroleum Co.

It said that under the contract, it will explore for oil and gas the Keta Block, located on the Volta River delta of Ghana's eastern coastal area, about 100 kilometers east of the capital city, Accra.
The Keta Block covers approximately 10,500 square kilometers (2.5 million acres), 80 percent of which lies offshore, it said. The area is its first work contract in Ghana, it said.
Santa Fe Energy Resources of Ghana, a wholly owned subsidiary of the U.S. company, holds 100 percent of the working interest in the Keta Block.
The U.S. company said it has committed to a three year work program during which it expects to spend at least $10 million.
It said the contract will become effective after ratification by Ghana's parliament.
It said that with the contract, it now holds interests in five offshore blocks in three West African countries, including Gabon and Ivory Coast.
James Payne, chairman and chief executive officer of Santa Fe Energy, said the contract terms "will make discoveries attractive not only to the people of Ghana but to our stockholders as well."
